steps.say: A composite solid is two shapes joined. Find each volume, then add. The new move: split into parts.

steps.done: 128π = 402.1 cm³. The new move: split, then add.

steps.say: Volume of a cuboid is length × width × height. Let us fill one in.

steps.pre: How many 1 cm cubes fill it?
steps.done: 42 cubes. That was the whole point: multiply all three lengths.

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the volume of a cuboid 7 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm.

steps.say: Volume of a cone is \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). The new move is that ⅓.

steps.done: V = 339.3 cm³. The new move: the ⅓ a cone always needs.

silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cone has radius 6 cm and height 9 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

steps.pre: The front face is 4 across and 3 high. How many cubes fill it? 4 × 3 =

steps.say: The tray is 2 cubes deep, so there is a second identical layer behind the front.

You just found a volume. Counting the 1 cm cubes that fill a shape IS its volume, and the shortcut is length × width × height = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cm³. Every formula today (cylinders, cones, spheres) is just a cleverer way of counting the space inside.

opener.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A tray is being packed with 1 cm sugar cubes. The front face fills up 4 cubes across and 3 cubes high, and the tray is 2 cubes deep.

steps: Identify the 3D shape and pick the right formula
For a prism, find the cross-section area first, then multiply by the length
Substitute carefully: watch radius vs diameter, and the ⅓ for cones and pyramids
Calculate and give units (cm³ for volume, cm² for surface area)
method_card.title: Volume & Surface Area
method_card.content:
Prism: V = cross-section area × length. Cuboid: V = \(lwh\), SA = \(2(lw + lh + wh)\). Cylinder: V = \(\pi r^2 h\), SA = \(2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh\).

Cone: V = \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). Pyramid: V = \(\frac{1}{3}\times\) base area \(\times h\). Sphere: V = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), SA = \(4\pi r^2\).
method_card.example:
Volume of a cylinder: radius 5 cm, height 12 cm.

V = \(\pi \times 5^2 \times 12 = 300\pi \approx 942.5\) cm³

steps: Sphere: V = \(\frac{4}{3}\)πr³, SA = 4πr². Composite: split into basic shapes, then add (joined) or subtract (a piece removed).
Keep each part in multiples of π until the final line, then round once.
Rearrange: to find a length from a given volume or area, substitute and solve, cancelling π where you can.
gold.title: Gold: spheres, composite solids and rearranging formulae

example.question: A hemisphere has radius 3 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

steps: Cuboid: volume = length × width × height. Cube: volume = side³.
Surface area: add the area of every face. A cube is 6 × side²; a cuboid is 2(lw + lh + wh).
bronze.title: Bronze: volume and surface area of basic solids

example.question: Find the volume of a cuboid 4 cm × 3 cm × 5 cm.

steps: Cylinder: V = π r² h. Cone: V = ⅓ π r² h. Pyramid: V = ⅓ × base area × h.
A hemisphere is half a sphere, so halve the sphere volume \(\frac{4}{3}\)πr³.
Reverse: to find a missing length, substitute the numbers and rearrange. Working in multiples of π keeps it exact.
silver.title: Silver: cones, spheres, pyramids and reverse problems

example.question: A cone has radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

gold.hint: Volume of a sphere is four thirds of π r³. Cube the radius first.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the volume of a sphere with radius 9 cm. Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a sphere is \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). Cube the radius first.

guided_steps.pre: Multiply by π and round: 972 × π =
Check in one go: \(\frac{4}{3}\) × π × 729 rounds to

misconceptions.message: Include the four thirds: V = \(\frac{4}{3}\) × π × 9³ = 972π = 3054 cm³, not just πr³.
That is close to the surface area (4πr²). Volume = \(\frac{4}{3}\)πr³ = 972π = 3054 cm³.

gold.hint: Surface area of a sphere is 4 π r². Square the radius first.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the surface area of a sphere with radius 5 cm. Give your answer to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Surface area of a sphere is \(4\pi r^2\). Square the radius first.

misconceptions.message: That is the volume. Surface area = 4πr² = 4 × π × 25 = 100π = 314.2 cm².
Surface area is 4πr², not πr² (that is one circle): 100π = 314.2 cm².

gold.hint: Volume of a sphere is \(\frac{4}{3}\)πr³. Work in π units, then take the cube root.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A sphere has volume \(\frac{256}{3}\pi\) cm³. Find the radius.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a sphere is \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). Set \(\frac{4}{3}r^3 = \frac{256}{3}\) in π units.

guided_steps.done: That is \(\frac{256}{3}\)π, matching, so r = 4 cm.

misconceptions.message: 64 is r³, not r. Take the cube root: r = ∛64 = 4 cm.
Cube root, not square root: r³ = 64, so r = ∛64 = 4 cm.

gold.hint: Cylinder volume minus cone volume. A cone is one third of the cylinder.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cone and a cylinder both have radius 5 cm and height 12 cm. How much more volume does the cylinder have? Give your answer to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: The cone is \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the cylinder, so the difference is \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the cylinder. Work in π units.

guided_steps.done: So the cylinder has 628.3 cm³ more.

misconceptions.message: That is the cone's volume. The extra = cylinder − cone = 300π − 100π = 200π = 628.3 cm³.
That is the whole cylinder. The extra is cylinder − cone = 200π = 628.3 cm³.

gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A solid is a cylinder (radius 3 cm, height 10 cm) with a hemisphere (radius 3 cm) on top. Find the total volume. Give your answer to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Total volume = cylinder + hemisphere on top. Work each in π units, then add.

misconceptions.message: Add the hemisphere on top: cylinder 90π + hemisphere 18π = 108π = 339.3 cm³.
The top is a HALF sphere, not a whole one: 90π + 18π = 108π = 339.3 cm³.

bronze.hint: Volume of a cuboid is length × width × height.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the volume of a cuboid with length 6 cm, width 4 cm and height 3 cm.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cuboid is length × width × height. Multiply all three.

misconceptions.message: 108 cm² is the surface area, 2(lw + lh + wh). Volume is 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cm³.
Multiply the three lengths, do not add: 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cm³.

bronze.hint: Volume of a cube is side × side × side.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the volume of a cube with side length 5 cm.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cube is side × side × side.

guided_steps.pre: Compare: the surface area would be 6 × 25 =
guided_steps.done: 150 is the surface area; the volume is 125 cm³.

misconceptions.message: Cube the side, do not square it: 5³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cm³.
150 cm² is the surface area (6 × 5²). Volume = 5³ = 125 cm³.

bronze.hint: Volume of any prism is the cross-section area times the length.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A triangular prism has cross-section area 20 cm² and length 9 cm. Find its volume.

guided_steps.say: Volume of any prism is the cross-section area times the length.

guided_steps.done: Back to the 20 cm² cross-section, so V = 180 cm³.

misconceptions.message: Multiply, do not add: volume of a prism = cross-section area × length = 20 × 9 = 180 cm³.
The cross-section area is already given as 20. Do not halve it again: 20 × 9 = 180 cm³.

bronze.hint: A cube has 6 identical square faces: find one, then times by 6.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the surface area of a cube with side length 4 cm.

guided_steps.say: A cube has 6 identical square faces. Find one face, then multiply by 6.

guided_steps.done: 64 is the volume; the surface area is 96 cm².

misconceptions.message: 64 cm³ is the volume (4³). Surface area = 6 × 4² = 6 × 16 = 96 cm².
A cube has 6 faces, not one: SA = 6 × 4² = 96 cm².

bronze.hint: Volume of a cuboid is length × width × height.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cuboid is 10 cm by 5 cm by 2 cm. Find its volume.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cuboid is length × width × height. Multiply all three.

misconceptions.message: Multiply, do not add: 10 × 5 × 2 = 100 cm³.
160 cm² is the surface area. Volume = 10 × 5 × 2 = 100 cm³.

bronze.hint: Find the cross-section area (6 × 3) first, then multiply by the length.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A prism has a rectangular cross-section 6 cm by 3 cm and is 15 cm long. Find its volume.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a prism is the cross-section area times the length. The cross-section here is a 6 by 3 rectangle.

guided_steps.done: Back to the 18 cm² cross-section, so V = 270 cm³.

misconceptions.message: That is just the cross-section area. Multiply by the length: 18 × 15 = 270 cm³.
Multiply, do not add: (6 × 3) × 15 = 270 cm³.

bronze.hint: Cube root: find the number that, cubed, gives 27.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cube has volume 27 cm³. Find the side length.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cube is side³, so we need the number whose cube is 27.

misconceptions.message: Do not divide by 3. Find the cube root: 3³ = 27, so the side is 3 cm.
Do not divide by 2. Take the cube root: 3³ = 27, so the side is 3 cm.

bronze.hint: 1 litre fills a cube 10 cm on every side.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately How many cm³ are there in 1 litre?

guided_steps.say: 1 litre is exactly the space inside a cube 10 cm on every side. Count the cm³ cubes.

misconceptions.message: 1 litre = 1000 cm³. A 10 cm cube holds 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000.
1 litre = 1000 cm³, not 10 000.

silver.hint: Volume of a cylinder is π r² h. Square the radius first.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. Give your answer to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cylinder is \(\pi r^2 h\). Square the radius first.

guided_steps.hint: Use the π button, round to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.pre: Check in one go: π × 4² × 10 rounds to

misconceptions.message: The radius must be squared: V = π × 4² × 10 = 160π = 502.7 cm³, not π × 4 × 10.

silver.hint: Volume of a cone is one third of π r² h.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the volume of a cone with radius 3 cm and height 7 cm. Give your answer to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cone is \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). Build \(\pi r^2 h\), then take a third.

guided_steps.pre: Check in one go: ⅓ × π × 9 × 7 rounds to

misconceptions.message: That is the full cylinder. A cone is one third: V = ⅓ × π × 3² × 7 = 21π = 66.0 cm³.
Square the radius: V = ⅓ × π × 3² × 7 = 21π = 66.0 cm³.

silver.hint: Volume of a pyramid is one third of base area × height.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A pyramid has a square base of side 6 cm and height 8 cm. Find its volume.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a pyramid is \(\frac{1}{3} \times\) base area \(\times h\). Find the base area first.

misconceptions.message: That is base area × height with no third. A pyramid is one third: V = ⅓ × 36 × 8 = 96 cm³.
Use the base AREA (6 × 6 = 36), not the side: V = ⅓ × 36 × 8 = 96 cm³.

silver.hint: Surface area of a cylinder is 2πr² (two ends) + 2πrh (curved part).
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the total surface area of a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. Give your answer to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Surface area of a cylinder is \(2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h\). Work in multiples of π, then multiply once.

guided_steps.pre: The two ends, 2πr², in π units: 2 × 3² =
The curved part, 2πrh, in π units: 2 × 3 × 10 =

misconceptions.message: Add the two circular ends too: SA = 2πr² + 2πrh = 18π + 60π = 78π = 245.0 cm².
That is only the two ends. Add the curved part 2πrh = 60π: total 78π = 245.0 cm².

silver.hint: Volume of a cylinder is πr²h. Work in multiples of π; the π cancels.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cylinder has volume \(500\pi\) cm³ and radius 10 cm. Find its height.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cylinder is \(\pi r^2 h\). Work in π units so the π cancels.

guided_steps.pre: Check: π × 10² × 5 in π units is 100 × 5 =

misconceptions.message: Square the radius: 500π = π × 10² × h = 100πh, so h = 500 ÷ 100 = 5 cm.

silver.hint: A hemisphere is half a sphere: find the full sphere, then halve it.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the volume of a hemisphere with radius 6 cm. Give your answer to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: A hemisphere is half a sphere. Find the full sphere's volume, then halve it.

guided_steps.pre: Check in one go: \(\frac{2}{3}\) × π × 216 rounds to

misconceptions.message: A hemisphere is HALF a sphere: V = ½ × \(\frac{4}{3}\) × π × 6³ = 144π = 452.4 cm³. The full sphere (904.8) is double.
Cube the radius, do not square it: V = ½ × \(\frac{4}{3}\) × π × 6³ = 144π = 452.4 cm³.

silver.hint: Find the trapezium area, ½(a + b)h, then multiply by the length.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A prism has a trapezium cross-section with parallel sides 5 cm and 9 cm and height 4 cm. The prism is 12 cm long. Find its volume.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a prism is cross-section area × length. First find the trapezium area, \(\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h\).

misconceptions.message: That is just the cross-section area. Multiply by the length: 28 × 12 = 336 cm³.
Trapezium area is ½(a + b)h. Do not drop the ½: area = 28, so V = 28 × 12 = 336 cm³.
